title: sessions.createOptions
description: The hub's (plan 036 §3.4): what a session.create can start on this machine, before any session exists — the agent providers with their availability, the default provider, and the directories sessions last ran in. It takes nothing (a member is bad_request, reason unknown_field) and is a read: neither session-scoped nor mutating. Every call recomputes it; nothing is cached. A state marks and never refuses: session.create starts a provider whatever its state. A host answers unsupported, reason hub_only; the connection capability createOptions says a hub serves it, and a hub that cannot answer it refuses it unsupported, reason unsupported.

providers.description: The agent providers this machine lists, in craze's registry order (cursor, grok, gx, native): gx only when its binary is found. Each provider's binary is resolved as a host the hub creates resolves it — [agents] in the hub's config.toml, then PATH — and native and the macOS login session are the hub's own, which its hosts inherit.

defaultProvider.description: The provider a session.create that names none starts: provider in the hub's config.toml (the one the last session to start persisted). Absent when none is set, or when it names no provider craze knows. It may name a provider that is not listed (a missing gx) or not ready.

recentDirs.description: The directories sessions ran in, newest first, from the hub's session index: distinct once cleaned, absolute, and still directories. [] for none, and when the index cannot be read (the hub logs why).

providerOption.description: One agent provider: its id (what session.create's provider takes), its label (what a client shows), its state and — present exactly when the state is not ready — why it cannot start and what to do about it. craze providers --json prints the same objects.

reason.description: Why it cannot start, as a row fact's text is cut: one line of at most 200 terminal cells. It names a file, never its content.

fix.description: What to do about it, as a row fact's text is cut: one line of at most 200 terminal cells.

providerState.description: ready: it can start here. needs_setup: it cannot start until something craze can lead a person through is set up — native with no model whose provider has a key (craze auth login funds one). unavailable: it cannot start, and nothing in craze can make it — its binary is not found, cursor runs outside the macOS login session (over ssh), or native's model files cannot be read.

recentDir.description: A directory sessions ran in, and when one last did.

dir.description: An absolute path to a directory that existed as the hub answered.

usedAt.description: The newest session index row's update time for the directory, in UTC.
